title: Optimization of the NFκB-DNA ensemble leads to high affinity binding of partial consensus sites
authors: Tristan R. Gunther; Sophia Hofmeister; Luke Sebastian; Hannah E.R. Baughman; Neville P. Bethel; Elizabeth A. Komives
one_liner_zh: 该文结合HDX-MS与MD模拟研究NFκB(RelA/p50)对部分一致序列DNA的高亲和结合机制，揭示结合口袋内DNA位置重排的动态互作机理，核心聚焦TF-DNA结合与动态机制，高度匹配本课题。
abstract: Our ability to respond to a myriad of external stressors is dependent on the activity of specific transcription factors that precisely regulate gene expression. While some transcription factors have high specificity for their consensus DNA binding site, others such as NFκB (RelA/p50) readily bind to partial and nonconsensus sites. In fact, ChIP-Seq data shows that nearly half of the DNA-bound RelA occupies sequences that do not match the consensus. Here we explore how NFκB (RelA/p50) binds to alternative sequences that differ subtly from the consensus. The two subunits of the NFκB heterodimer, RelA and p50, form an extensive pocket where DNA binding is mediated by both base-specific contacts and nonspecific interactions with the DNA backbone. RelA and p50 each form sequence-specific contacts with DNA at different 4-nucleotide sequences separated by two nucleotides, together forming a 10-base pair consensus binding sequence. Partial consensus sequences, known as half-sites, match the consensus sequence at only one of these two 4-nucleotide interaction sites. Here, using hydrogen deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDX-MS) and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to investigate protein structural dynamics, we observe that rearranging nucleotides at the RelA-interacting end of a consensus DNA sequence to form a half-site induces dynamic structural changes through both subunits of RelA/p50. MD simulations reveal a shift in the position of DNA within the RelA/p50 binding pocket that allows optimal interaction with the half-site sequence. Our results demonstrate how RelA/p50 fine-tunes its interactions to achieve high-affinity binding with multiple different target DNA sequences.
abstract_zh: 我们应对众多外部应激源的能力，依赖于精确调控基因表达的特定转录因子的活性。虽然一些转录因子对其共识DNA结合位点具有高度特异性，但其他如NFκB（RelA/p50）则易于结合部分和非共识位点。事实上，ChIP-Seq数据显示，近一半的DNA结合RelA占据的序列与共识序列不匹配。在此，我们探讨NFκB（RelA/p50）如何结合与共识序列微妙不同的替代序列。NFκB异二聚体的两个亚基RelA和p50形成一个广泛的凹槽，其中DNA结合通过碱基特异性接触和与DNA骨架的非特异性相互作用介导。RelA和p50各自与DNA上相隔两个核苷酸的不同4核苷酸序列形成序列特异性接触，共同构成一个10碱基对的共识结合序列。部分共识序列，称为半位点，仅在这两个4核苷酸相互作用位点之一与共识序列匹配。这里，我们使用氢氘交换质谱（HDX-MS）和分子动力学（molecular dynamics）模拟来研究蛋白质结构动态，观察到将共识DNA序列的RelA相互作用端核苷酸重排以形成半位点，会诱导RelA/p50两个亚基的结构动态变化。MD模拟揭示了DNA在RelA/p50结合凹槽内位置的移动，这允许与半位点序列实现最佳相互作用。我们的结果展示了RelA/p50如何微调其相互作用，以实现与多种不同靶DNA序列的高亲和力结合。
